profile.name: LabTrack LIMS
profile.business_function: Laboratory Information Management System for QC release testing of finished drug product
profile.description: Tracks samples from receipt through testing, results review and Certificate of Analysis (CoA) generation. Used by QC labs to release batches. Results feed batch disposition decisions, so the system is GxP-critical and was validated under GAMP 5 (Category 4 with Category 5 customisations).
profile.tech_stack: ASP.NET WebForms on .NET Framework 4.5, C#, jQuery 1.8, Crystal Reports 13 for CoA PDFs, log4net. A Windows Service polls an SMB share for instrument result files (HPLC/Empower exports as CSV).
profile.database: SQL Server 2012 Standard, ~600 GB, ~400 stored procedures with business logic, nightly full backup to tape
profile.hosting: On-premises: 2 IIS web servers (Windows Server 2012 R2) behind a hardware load balancer with sticky sessions, 1 SQL Server cluster, 1 instrument-integration server
profile.integrations: SAP ECC (batch master data via nightly flat-file export), Empower CDS (CSV file drop on SMB share), Active Directory (Windows authentication), SMTP for result notifications
profile.users: ~350 QC analysts and reviewers across 3 manufacturing sites; peak load during month-end batch release
profile.data_classification: GxP electronic records subject to 21 CFR Part 11 and EU Annex 11; audit trail and electronic signatures on result approval; 10+ year retention
profile.pain_points: Windows Server 2012 R2 and SQL Server 2012 are out of support; audit findings on unpatched servers; month-end slowdowns; adding a new site takes 3 months; only 2 developers understand the stored procedures
profile.constraints: Validated state must be preserved; no unplanned downtime during batch release windows; data must stay in the EU for the Ireland site

summary.headline: Replatform LabTrack onto Azure PaaS in about 30 weeks, then strangle instrument ingestion and reporting into cloud-native services - preserving validated state through a risk-based IQ/OQ/PQ plan.
top_risks: Loss of validated state during migration
Hidden business logic in stored procedures

architecture.architecture_style: 3-tier Windows monolith (ASP.NET WebForms + stored-procedure business logic)
architecture.summary: A server-rendered WebForms application on two sticky-session IIS servers, backed by a SQL Server 2012 database that holds most business rules in ~400 stored procedures. Instrument results arrive as CSV files on an SMB share and are polled by a separate Windows Service. Every core platform layer is past end of support.

components.name: LabTrack Web Portal
components.description: Sample login, result entry, review/approval with e-signatures, CoA requests.
issues: In-process session state forces sticky sessions
Business rules duplicated between code-behind and stored procedures

components.name: LabTrack Database
components.description: System of record for samples, results, specifications and audit trail.
issues: Nightly tape backup gives a 24-hour RPO

components.name: Instrument Integration Service
components.technology: Windows Service (.NET 4.5) polling an SMB share
components.description: Parses Empower CSV exports every 5 minutes and inserts results.

components.name: CoA Report Engine
components.technology: Crystal Reports 13 runtime on the web servers
components.description: Generates Certificate of Analysis PDFs for batch release.
issues: 32-bit runtime pins reporting to the IIS hosts
Validated templates - any change needs OQ re-execution

components.name: Instrument Drop Share
components.description: Landing folder for instrument result files.
issues: Files can be edited or deleted before ingestion
No checksums - an ALCOA+ data integrity gap

components.name: Empower CDS
components.description: Chromatography data system in each lab.

components.name: SAP ECC
components.description: Source of batch and material master data.
issues: Overnight latency for newly created batches

components.name: Active Directory
components.description: User identity for login and e-signatures.

tech_inventory.name: .NET Framework
tech_inventory.note: 4.5.2 support ended April 2022; retarget to 4.8 is low effort

tech_inventory.name: ASP.NET WebForms
tech_inventory.note: Frozen technology - runs only on .NET Framework 4.8, no port to modern .NET

tech_inventory.name: IIS
tech_inventory.note: Lifecycle tied to Windows Server 2012 R2

tech_inventory.name: jQuery
tech_inventory.note: Known XSS issues fixed only in 3.5+

tech_inventory.name: Crystal Reports runtime
tech_inventory.note: Confirm vendor support; 32-bit runtime constrains hosting

tech_debt: Core result calculations and specification checks live in ~400 stored procedures with no automated tests
In-process session state requires sticky sessions and blocks horizontal scaling
Hard-coded UNC paths and connection strings in configuration
No CI/CD pipeline - releases are manual with paper-based IQ evidence
Each release re-executes ~300 manual OQ test scripts
architecture.regulated_data: QC test results, sample chain of custody, analyst e-signatures on result approval and the CoAs used for batch release - GxP electronic records under 21 CFR Part 11 / EU Annex 11 with 10+ year retention.

dimensions.label: Technology currency
dimensions.rationale: Every core platform layer (OS, database, framework) is past end of support.
evidence: Windows Server 2012 R2 - extended support ended Oct 2023
SQL Server 2012 - extended support ended Jul 2022
.NET Framework 4.5 target
jQuery 1.8.3 with known XSS CVEs

dimensions.label: Modularity & coupling
dimensions.rationale: Monolithic WebForms app, but instrument integration and reporting already run as separate processes - natural seams for a strangler approach.
evidence: Instrument integration is a separate Windows Service
Business logic split between code-behind and stored procedures

dimensions.label: Statelessness & scalability
dimensions.rationale: In-process session state and sticky sessions allow vertical scaling only; month-end peaks cause slowdowns.
evidence: sessionState mode=InProc
Hardware load balancer with sticky sessions
Month-end batch-release slowdowns

dimensions.label: Data portability
dimensions.rationale: SQL Server maps cleanly to Azure SQL Managed Instance; 600 GB is manageable and stored procedures port unchanged.
evidence: SQL Server 2012 Standard, ~600 GB
T-SQL stored procedures are compatible with Azure SQL Managed Instance

dimensions.label: Integration complexity
dimensions.rationale: Only four integrations, but two are file-based and must be redesigned for the cloud.
evidence: Empower CSV file drop on SMB share
SAP ECC nightly flat file
Windows authentication via Active Directory

dimensions.label: Compliance & validation
dimensions.rationale: GxP-critical with Part 11 e-signatures; any platform change needs risk-based re-validation, cloud supplier qualification and EU residency controls.
evidence: GAMP 5 Category 4/5 validated system
21 CFR Part 11 audit trail and e-signatures
EU data residency for the Ireland site

dimensions.label: DevOps maturity
dimensions.rationale: Manual deployments, tape backups and no automated tests; every release re-runs manual OQ scripts.
evidence: Nightly full backup to tape
Only 2 developers understand the stored procedures
No CI/CD configuration found

risks.title: Loss of validated state during migration
risks.description: Moving OS, database and hosting invalidates existing IQ evidence; without a risk-based re-validation plan the system cannot be used for batch release.
risks.mitigation: Risk-based CSA plan: re-execute IQ on new infrastructure, targeted OQ on changed functions, PQ via parallel run across two batch-release cycles, QA sign-off gate before cutover.

risks.title: Unpatched end-of-life platform
risks.description: Windows Server 2012 R2 and SQL Server 2012 receive no security updates and are already an audit finding.
risks.mitigation: Make platform exit the wave-1 driver; isolate the servers in a restricted network segment until cutover.

risks.title: Hidden business logic in stored procedures
risks.description: ~400 undocumented stored procedures hold validated calculations; refactoring could silently change results.
risks.mitigation: Replatform procedures unchanged to Azure SQL Managed Instance; add characterisation tests before any refactor.

risks.title: Key-person dependency
risks.description: Only two developers understand the stored procedures and the integration service.
risks.mitigation: Embed both in the migration team from week 1 and document critical procedures during assessment.

risks.title: Instrument file integrity gap
risks.description: CSV files on the SMB share can be altered or deleted before ingestion and are not checksummed - an ALCOA+ gap.
risks.mitigation: Event-driven ingestion that hashes files on arrival, stores originals in immutable storage and writes an audit-trail entry.

risks.title: Cutover collides with batch release
risks.description: Downtime during month-end batch release would delay product release.
risks.mitigation: Mid-month cutover window, online migration with log-backup replay, rehearsed rollback plan.

risks.title: Cloud supplier not yet qualified
risks.description: GxP requires assessing the cloud provider as a supplier with a defined shared-responsibility model.
risks.mitigation: Use the provider's GxP guidance and audit reports (SOC 2, ISO 27001), sign a quality agreement and map shared responsibility in the validation plan.

risks.title: EU data residency breach
risks.description: Ireland-site records must stay in the EU; a single global deployment could breach residency commitments.
risks.mitigation: Deploy to an EU region with an allowed-locations policy and document data flows in the validation plan.

opportunities.title: Retire tape backups
opportunities.benefit: Automated geo-redundant backups with point-in-time restore cut RPO from 24 hours to minutes.

opportunities.title: Elastic capacity for month-end
opportunities.benefit: Scale the web tier out during batch release, ending month-end slowdowns.

opportunities.title: Validation as code
opportunities.benefit: Automated regression tests and infrastructure-as-code turn ~300 manual OQ scripts into repeatable evidence, in line with FDA's Computer Software Assurance approach.

opportunities.title: Onboard new sites in weeks
opportunities.benefit: A templated landing zone shrinks new-site onboarding from 3 months to a few weeks.

opportunities.title: Near real-time instrument results
opportunities.benefit: Event-driven ingestion delivers results in seconds and closes the data integrity gap.

plan.headline: Replatform LabTrack onto Azure PaaS in about 30 weeks, then strangle instrument ingestion and reporting into cloud-native services - preserving validated state through a risk-based IQ/OQ/PQ plan.

patterns.name: Replatform to managed PaaS
patterns.why: Fastest exit from the end-of-life OS and database while keeping validated stored-procedure logic unchanged.

patterns.name: Strangler fig
patterns.why: Peel off instrument ingestion and CoA reporting after the platform move, re-validating only what changes.

patterns.name: Event-driven ingestion
patterns.why: Replaces SMB polling with blob events, adding hashing and immutable storage for ALCOA+.

patterns.name: Externalised session state
patterns.why: Moving session state to a managed cache removes sticky sessions and enables scale-out.

component_strategies.rationale: Retarget to .NET Framework 4.8 and run on App Service; minimal code change keeps OQ scope small.
Near-full SQL Server compatibility keeps all stored procedures unchanged, with built-in HA and point-in-time restore.
Replace the polling Windows Service with event-driven ingestion that checksums files and writes audit entries.
Keep validated CoA templates during waves 1-2 to avoid re-validating report output; modernise reporting in the final phase.
component_strategies.target_service: App Service, then Power BI paginated reports

component_strategies.rationale: Replaced by an immutable blob landing container with checksums.
Empower stays on-premises in the labs; an upload agent sends exports to Azure over private connectivity.
SAP is out of scope; replace the flat-file hand-off with a scheduled pipeline.
Hybrid identity keeps unique user IDs for Part 11 and adds MFA on e-signatures.
A managed email service replaces the on-premises relay.

plan.target_summary: Azure PaaS in an EU region inside a GxP landing zone: App Service web tier with Redis session state, Azure SQL Managed Instance, event-driven instrument ingestion through Functions and immutable Blob Storage, Entra ID for identity, and Azure Monitor / Log Analytics for audit-grade logging.

target_components.name: Instrument Ingestion
target_components.description: Hashes, validates and loads result files; writes audit entries.

target_components.name: Raw Results Vault
target_components.description: WORM copy of every original instrument file.

target_components.name: CoA Reporting
target_components.description: Validated CoA templates after the final phase.

target_components.name: Identity
target_components.description: SSO with MFA on e-signature events.

target_components.name: Audit & Monitoring
target_components.description: Centralised, retained audit and application logs.

roadmap.name: Assess and validation planning
objectives: Agree the validation strategy with QA
activities: Inventory stored procedures and integrations
GxP impact assessment and risk-based validation plan (CSA approach)
Cloud supplier qualification and quality agreement
Define cutover and rollback windows around batch release

roadmap.name: Landing zone and foundation
objectives: Stand up a qualified, EU-resident platform
activities: EU-region landing zone with policies for allowed locations, encryption and tagging
Hub-spoke network and site-to-site VPN to the labs
Entra ID hybrid sync and MFA
Infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD pipelines with approval gates

roadmap.name: Pilot - database and web replatform
objectives: Prove the replatformed stack in a validated test environment
activities: Retarget the web app to .NET Framework 4.8 and move session state to Redis
Migrate a database copy to Azure SQL Managed Instance
Automate the top 50 OQ scripts as regression tests
Load-test month-end batch release volumes

roadmap.name: Event-driven instrument ingestion
objectives: Close the ALCOA+ gap on instrument data
activities: Build Functions ingestion with SHA-256 hashing and immutable storage
Parallel-run with the legacy Windows Service and reconcile results
Update data integrity SOPs

roadmap.name: Production cutover and PQ
objectives: Go live without disrupting batch release
activities: Online data migration with log-backup replay and mid-month cutover
Parallel run across two batch-release cycles
Hypercare with a rehearsed rollback plan

roadmap.name: Optimise and decommission
objectives: Retire legacy infrastructure and lock in savings
activities: Decommission on-premises servers and archive tape data per the retention policy
Move CoA reporting to Power BI paginated reports
Autoscale rules and cost optimisation
Hand over to cloud operations with periodic review

quick_wins: Upgrade jQuery to 3.5+ and isolate the end-of-life servers in a restricted network segment now
Start automating the top 50 manual OQ scripts - reusable on any platform
Add SHA-256 checksums to instrument file drops to close the ALCOA+ gap immediately
Document the 20 most critical stored procedures with the two key developers
